clue.text: Control south-eastern part of the country, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase says the region's name is only heard, so it is spelt as a different word that is pronounced alike

parts.note: the Weald is a once-wooded area of Kent and Sussex in south-east England

explanation.surface: A remark about governing a corner of England, with a nod to how it is pronounced.
explanation.walkthrough: THE WEALD is a region of south-east England; said aloud it matches the word meaning to handle or exercise power.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield power is to exercise control over something.

clue.text: Bowdlerise novel, deleting mention of ship

indicators.note: deleting mention of says a word is cut out of the title

parts.note: Watership Down is Richard Adams's novel about rabbits
taken as written

explanation.surface: Censoring a book by cutting out all references to a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowdlerise is to censor a text, weakening it by removing offending parts.

clue.text: Turned up some information about new recruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up says the letters are read from the bottom upwards
about says the word for information goes around the letter

parts.note: lore is a body of knowledge or information

explanation.surface: Uncovering details about a new hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside LORE to make LORNE, which 'Turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone is to sign them up as a member.

clue.text: When work is stopped rebuilding town, outside money is required

indicators.note: outside says the coin word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin

indicators.note: rebuilding says the word town is reconstructed in a new order

explanation.surface: Reconstruction of a town paused until funds arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When work is stopped' is the definition, not part of the instructions; 'rebuilding' signals the anagram, 'outside' the container, and 'is required' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A period when machines or staff are idle is time off production.

clue.text: Unique end to final in dull game

parts.note: mat (or matt) describes a dull, unshiny finish

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for the game

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: end to picks the last letter of the word final

explanation.surface: A sports report calling a decisive finish to a boring contest one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull game' tempts as a phrase, but 'dull' and 'game' are separate pieces; 'end to' takes the last letter of 'final', and 'in' puts it inside the game after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique has no equal, nothing to match it.

clue.text: Poor design

explanation.surface: A curt verdict on a bad plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean means shabby or inferior, and to design something can mean to intend it.

clue.text: Chinese get scared and run away

indicators.note: relies on the old caricature of Chinese speakers swapping the letter R for L

parts.note: to take fright is to become frightened

explanation.surface: A Chinese person panicking and fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: A dated clue built on a stereotype: 'Chinese' turns TAKE FRIGHT into a version with L for R.
explanation.definitionFit: To take flight means to flee, to escape by running off.

clue.text: Limp pocket books inside

indicators.note: inside says the books abbreviation sits within the word for pocket

parts.note: a pocket can be a hole, as in a pocket of air
B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: An instruction to stuff books into a floppy pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to walk awkwardly, with a limp.

clue.text: Thinking a lot of points on streaming

indicators.note: in a down clue, on says this piece sits above the next one

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south
teeming means pouring or streaming down

explanation.surface: Musing on the main ideas of online streaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteeming someone is holding them in high regard.

clue.text: Fish ponged

explanation.surface: A fish that stank.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelt is a small silvery fish, and smelt is also a past tense meaning gave off a bad odour.

clue.text: Revert to type, producing slipshod work with batch

indicators.note: slipshod means careless and disordered, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Careless output from a factory batch shows things going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipshod' rearranges WORK and BATCH together; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw back is to show traits of an ancestor, reverting to an earlier type.

clue.text: Cricketer-a man in the swim

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer who bats
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A cricketer who also goes in for swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: BAT is crossword shorthand for a batsman in cricket; in British usage 'a bathe' is a dip or swim in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathe, in British usage, is a short swim, as in a dip in the sea.

clue.text: Couple set forth

explanation.surface: Two people setting off together on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple ideas is to connect them, and to set forth a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: A fellow smooth-tongued and well-heeled

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
a smooth-tongued speaker talks fluently

explanation.surface: A portrait of a glib, rich man.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an idiom for rich, wealthy enough to afford good shoes.

clue.text: Watch part of pest menace being destroyed

indicators.note: being destroyed says the two words are broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a dangerous insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'being destroyed' rearranges PEST and MENACE.
explanation.definitionFit: This mechanism in a clock or watch regulates the movement, releasing the gear train step by step.

clue.text: Sanguine, despite one thing blurring vision in eye

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the word for an eye

parts.note: optic is a jocular word for an eye
the Roman numeral for one is I
mist blurs what one sees

explanation.surface: Someone staying cheerful though their eyesight is clouded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite' is only a link; 'in' puts the numeral and the fog word inside a jocular word for an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means hopeful and confident about the future.

clue.text: They say the stuff you contributed is scrappy

indicators.note: They say signals that the pieces are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: truck means stuff or goods, you is U, and contributed is lent

explanation.surface: Gossip that what you donated is pretty poor.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUCK (stuff) + U (you) + LENT (contributed) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrappy here means aggressive and ready to fight, which is to be belligerent.

clue.text: Face setback

indicators.note: back says the word for set is written in the other direction

parts.note: laid, as in laid the table, means set

explanation.surface: Confronting a reverse in fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' splits into 'set' (LAID) and 'back', which turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The dial of a clock or watch is its face.

clue.text: Secure rooms in hospital onshore

parts.note: to land a deal or prize is to secure it
wards are the rooms in a hospital where patients stay

explanation.surface: Booking hospital beds near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving onshore means heading towards the land from sea.

clue.text: With leader demoted, a cushy job is not cushy

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and demoted says it moves further down the word

parts.note: a sinecure is a paid post requiring little work

explanation.surface: A soft post losing its security once the boss is moved down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With leader demoted' moves the S of SINECURE down to third place; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means unsafe and precarious, the opposite of a safe comfortable position.

clue.text: Abroad, we show some sense

explanation.surface: Overseas travellers proving they have a bit of common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the pronoun for we is spelt this way, and in English the word is slang for practical intelligence.

clue.text: Maxim sister is about, for instance, to follow at high speed

indicators.note: to follow says this piece comes after the speed piece

parts.note: Mach one, the speed of sound, written MACH I with a Roman numeral

indicators.note: is about says the word for sister surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
eg (exempli gratia) means for instance

explanation.surface: A breathless account of a nun chasing something very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A Maxim was an early machine weapon named after its inventor Hiram Maxim; MACH I is Mach one, the speed of sound. 'is about' makes NEGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maxim was the first fully automatic firearm of its type, invented by Hiram Maxim.

clue.text: Rook left in position

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the word for position

parts.note: caste is a social rank or position

explanation.surface: A chess piece abandoned where it stood.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the rook is also known by another name for a fortified tower piece.

clue.text: Old campaigner found it rougher outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for rougher wraps around the other piece

parts.note: cruder means rougher, less refined
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A veteran discovering a place harsher outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention; 'outside' puts CRUDER around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval knight fighting for the Holy Land was one who went on campaign long ago.

clue.text: The best Conservative papers

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A boast about the finest Tory newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The top or choicest part of anything, as in the pick of the bunch.

clue.text: Connection with old book in novel

indicators.note: in places the book abbreviation inside the word for novel

parts.note: novel means new
Eph. is the abbreviation for Ephesians, an ancient book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A link found with an antique volume inside a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is the adjective, not a book; 'in' puts the abbreviation after the first letter of the adjective's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A connection can mean a relative, as a brother's son is a family relation.

clue.text: It's not, so to speak, a snag

definitions.text: It's not, so to speak, a snag

parts.words: It's not, so to speak, a snag
parts.note: said aloud, not is knot: a kind of knot that is also a word for a difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is both a type of knot and a minor obstacle or problem.

clue.text: In other words, an examination

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is used in texts to mean namely, in other words

explanation.surface: Rephrasing something as a test.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, short for Latin scilicet, introduces a clarification in a text, meaning namely.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is a medical examination by imaging, or a close inspection.

clue.text: Take part in seventeenth race

indicators.note: part in says a run of letters is taken from within the following word

explanation.surface: An invitation to compete in a seventeenth contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a link; the letters sit inside 'seventeenth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is one contest on an athletics programme, an item in a meeting.

clue.text: Truce none have broken in battle

indicators.note: have broken suggests the two words are smashed and their letters scattered

explanation.surface: A ceasefire collapsing so that fighting resumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have broken' rearranges TRUCE and NONE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a clash between opposing forces, a fight.

clue.text: Decrepit old bird accepts the honour

indicators.note: accepts says the bird takes the next word inside it

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct
in bridge and whist the ten is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: A feeble elderly person receiving an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honour' looks like a medal but is a card: the honours are ace, king, queen, jack and ten. 'accepts' puts the article inside the extinct bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten away by insects is worn-out and shabby, like decrepit old clothing.

clue.text: Those unusual national characteristics

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of the word are in an odd order

explanation.surface: Remarking on odd traits peculiar to a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A people's guiding spirit and character is its distinctive outlook.
